newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund details new commodities projects.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund details new commodities projects.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, said on Friday an executive board meeting this week decided financing on eight new projects covering the cocoa, coffee, zinc, cotton and coconut sectors.
The fund only part-finances projects, with the balance being provided by benefiting countries and other donors.
The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) has sponsored two five-year projects.
The first, with a budget of $3.2 million, aims to develop cocoa strains resistant to witches broom disease in Brazil.
The second, based at Rome's International Plant Genetic Resources Institute, has a total budget of $10.2 million to investigate making optimal use of cocoa germplasm.
There are two coffee projects sponsored by the International Coffee Organization (ICO), the first looking at ways to control coffee berry borer, a pest affecting 40 coffee growing nations.
With a budget of $5.5 million the project will be coordinated by the International Institute for Biological Control in the UK and carried out in Central America and India.
The second is a study of marketing and trading policies within liberalisation programmes undertaken by major coffee producers.
There are two zinc-related projects sponsored by the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (IZLG).
The first, with a budget of $156,000, aims to develop die casting techniques in the UK and the second, costing $217,000, looks at galvanizing applications in France.

The other two projects include a $2.1 million study into cotton stickiness, which severely disrupts the spinning process. It sponsored by the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) and will be conducted in Sudan.

The final project is $4.3 million study into improving the competitiveness of the coconut sector through new, higher yielding varieties. Sponsored by the FAO, it will be implemented in Africa, Latin America and the Pacific.
